items.title: UMK supports student who lost parents in Gerik crash
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) is providing welfare and psychological support to graduating student Husna Syakira Abd Halim, who lost her parents in a road crash. In a statement, UMK expressed its condolences and deep sorrow over the tragedy involving the Faculty of Entrepreneurship and Business student. UMK said it would continue to support the family, including with welfare assistance and other arrangements, to ensure everything ran smoothly.

items.title: NST Leader: When petrol pit stops prove perilous
items.summary: WAS it some weakness in the supply chain or unscrupulous businesses trying to cash in on our heavily subsidised RON95 petrol? The Petrol Dealers Association of Malaysia pointed out that it was counter-intuitive for petrol station owners to adulterate their petrol. Investigating authorities must establish whether the incidents are isolated cases of poor maintenance of underground storage tanks or weaknesses further up the supply chain.

items.title: Could hackers get inside my fridge?
items.summary: From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarm networks, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals. WHAT HOUSEHOLD DEVICES COULD BE HACKED? The most common targets are devices connected to the internet and controlled remotely.

items.title: Overseas missions generate RM59.5bil in potential investments, says Miti
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Fourteen official visits and trade and investment missions led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani generated RM59.5 billion in potential investments between 2025 and September this year. The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) said the missions were carried out through the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) and the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade). It added that markets which recorded double-digit growth included Namibia (up 426.1 per cent), Angola (55.6 per cent), Brazil (41.0 per cent), Tanzania (35.9 per cent), Ethiopia (28.5 per cent) and Kenya (11.6 per cent).

items.title: Fridge cyberattack hits supermarkets across Europe
items.summary: Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden were among those affected in the latest hacker attack. Major French retailers said on Oct 12 that hundreds of store refrigeration systems were hit by a cyberattack, which also forced them to toss food and raised concerns about food security. Carrefour Belgium on Monday reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores.

items.title: AI chatbots spewing US election falsehoods face scrutiny
items.summary: DISPENSING misleading voter information, misidentifying candidates and regurgitating Russian propaganda, artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are sowing information chaos ahead of the United States midterm elections, say researchers. Today's vote marks the first federal election in which millions of voters are actively relying on AI tools for political information, a trend that experts say is playing a key role in shaping the information ecosystem ahead of the polls. One recent study by Forum AI, a startup that evaluates AI models, found that almost 40 per cent of chatbots' answers to election-related queries contained at least one factual error.

items.title: More than 10,000 patients facing organ failure in Malaysia, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 10,036 patients in the country were facing organ failure as of Oct 15, underscoring the need for comprehensive reforms to the organ donation and transplant ecosystem, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said the need was increasingly urgent given the low rate of organ donation, at just 1.33 donors per million population. Dzulkefly said he chaired the council's first meeting this afternoon.

items.title: Melaka cops receive six election-related complaints
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka police have received six election-related reports since yesterday, including four involving damage to or the loss of political parties' campaign materials. Police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said the complaints involved campaign flags being broken, removed, torn, burnt and damaged in several state constituencies. Police also received reports of PH flags allegedly being removed in Ayer Limau and Parti Bersama campaign materials being damaged in Paya Rumput, he said in a statement.

items.title: Residents recount desperate escapes as flash floods hit Kampung Melayu Subang
items.summary: SUBANG: A man had to carry his elderly parents to safety after flash floods hit Kampung Melayu Subang oday, with floodwaters rising rapidly to waist level. Zulkarnain Hashim, 46, said he carried his 90-year-old mother and 89-year-old father to higher ground as the water surged. He said there was a heavy downpour from 2 pm to 4 pm, before water levels rose abruptly to waist level by 5pm.

items.title: Sri Lanka's war widows still search for the missing
items.summary: SEATED outside a church, Saradhadevi Thadcanamoorty recites four handwritten pages of names — 124 husbands, fathers and brothers who vanished during Sri Lanka's civil war. Tens of thousands also disappeared, or were abducted, tortured or killed by security forces or the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE). Witnesses said a soldier had killed him.

items.title: Five China nationals arrested over scam using women's profiles to target Germans
items.summary: IPOH: Police arrested five China nationals operating an investment scam syndicate targeting victims in Germany from a house in Anjung Bercham Utama. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, all men aged between 26 and 43, were detained following information received by police. "Based on initial investigations and conversation scripts found on seized computers, police believe the syndicate ran a call centre operation to carry out non-existent online investment scams.

items.title: Melaka polls: Bersama candidate claims party flags vandalised, one set ablaze
items.summary: Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar said party campaign workers discovered the damage between 4am and 7am yesterday. He said an inspection near the Jalan Bukit Rambai bridge found several flagpoles broken and one flag burnt. Meanwhile, Melaka police, when contacted, said they would issue a statement on the incident.

items.title: Loke credits federal-state cooperation for Sarawak transport projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Strong cooperation and a close working relationship between the federal government and the Sarawak government have delivered high-impact transport development projects in the state within a short period, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. These include support for the establishment of Sarawak's own airline, the handover of Bintulu Port Authority to the state government, the introduction of the BAS.MY (http://bas.my/) public transport system in Kuching, the upgrading of Miri Airport and the construction of a new Road Transport Department (RTD) complex in Limbang. On land transport, he said the ministry had provided direct funding for public transport in Sarawak, which had not previously received such funding.

items.title: Sabah's RM1.7bil rural road projects postponed, not cancelled, says Mustapha
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rural road development projects worth RM1.7 billion in Sabah have not been cancelled but postponed pending a review and realignment of allocation ceilings, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud. He said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan had provided a detailed explanation during the winding-up of the policy-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 last Thursday. The status of the projects had previously sparked controversy and questions following allegations of conflicting statements regarding the postponement of 13 rural road infrastructure projects, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Monday, Nov 2, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1569363]] [[nid:1569362]] [[nid:1569361]] [[nid:1569360]] [[nid:1569359]] [[nid:1569358]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Selangor police dispose of RM1.71bil worth of illicit drugs
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) disposed of 37.3 tonnes of illicit drugs of various types valued at RM1.71 billion today. Meanwhile, Hussein said 45.7 tonnes of solid drugs and 60,880 litres of liquid drugs worth approximately RM1.93 billion were disposed nationwide. Hussein said the NCID also disposed of 13,342 narcotics investigation papers nationwide involving cases from 1991 to 2025.

items.title: MoE steps up flood preparations for SPM candidates
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: The Education Ministry is stepping up preparations for the northeast monsoon to ensure Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas can sit their examinations safely. Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation, named Ops Payung, was aimed at ensuring candidates in flood-affected areas could take their examinations without disruption. He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations.

items.title: Police rule out racial, gang links in Desa Tun Razak clash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have ruled out racial and gang-related elements in a clash involving a group of people outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, last night. Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said preliminary investigations indicated that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a business turf dispute, although investigations were ongoing to determine the actual cause. Earlier, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that nine people had been arrested by a team from the Sungai Besi Police Station's Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit and the Cheras district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department.

items.title: US Senate confirms Joshua Harris as ambassador to Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The United States (US) Senate has confirmed the nomination of Joshua Harris as the country's next ambassador to Malaysia. Harris has been confirmed by the US Senate as the country's next ambassador to Malaysia, following a voice vote on Sept 30, 2026. According to the US Congress website, Harris, from Maryland, is a career member of the US Senior Foreign Service with the rank of Minister-Counsellor.

items.title: KTMB confirms cargo train locomotive catches fire in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has confirmed that a cargo train locomotive caught fire at Kilometre 4.75 along the Kempas Baru-Pasir Gudang route around 1.10 pm today. In a statement, KTMB said locomotive M1004 was hauling cargo train No. "The fire was completely extinguished by the Fire and Rescue Department at 2.50 pm.

items.title: Flash floods close both directions of NKVE between Shah Alam, Setia Alam
items.summary: Plus Malaysia Bhd said the closure involved both carriageways between Kilometre 9.1 and KM9.4, following heavy rain around 6.20pm. Highway users are advised to refer to Plus' official communication channels — X account @PLUSTrafik, the PLUS app, Variable Message Signs (VMS), Plus' virtual assistant PUTRI, and its official social media platforms - for the latest updates on weather and flood conditions, as well as alternative routes. For immediate assistance, highway users can contact PlusLine at 1-800-88-0000, use the SOS button on the Plus app or interact with Plus' virtual assistant, PUTRI.

items.title: Govt finalising Child Act amendments to set clearer detention periods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is finalising the draft Children (Amendment) Bill 2026 for submission to the cabinet for consideration, said Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M Kulasegaran. He said the proposed amendments aimed to improve Section 97 of the Child Act following the abolition of mandatory death sentences and life imprisonment in 2023. He said the changes would introduce a more proportionate sentencing framework and prevent juvenile offenders from being imprisoned indefinitely without a specified detention period.

items.title: Puchong slaughterhouse not under Jakim's halal monitoring, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A chicken slaughterhouse suspected of operating without local authority permits was not listed in the Department of Islamic Development (Jakim)'s monitoring records because it did not have halal certification. He said halal certification authority in Malaysia is governed under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 through the Trade Descriptions (Certification and Marking of Halal) Order 2011. Zulkifli said Jakim, together with State Islamic Religious Departments and State Islamic Religious Councils, enforces oversight through halal certification, audits, and monitoring of premises that hold the halal certification.

items.title: Strong winds rip roofs off houses in Kulim [WATCH]
items.summary: KULIM: About 10 houses in Taman Jati, Taman Selasih and Kampung Padang Kulim were damaged by strong winds during a storm in Kulim at about 4pm today. I saw many fallen trees and broken branches. He said five personnel were involved in cutting up and clearing fallen trees at locations beside Masjid Kulim, Kulim Avenue, Jalan Pegawai Kampung Bukit Awie, the Kulim District Office quarters and Taman Kenari.

items.title: Cop held over RM15,000 in bribes to protect drug trafficking activities
items.summary: Investigations indicated the offences took place throughout 2024. Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong confirmed the arrest. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Four vehicles, car workshop destroyed in Rembau fire
items.summary: REMBAU: Four vehicles and a car workshop were destroyed in a fire at Batu 17, Chembong. A Negri Sembilan Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said it received a call about the fire at a workshop opposite Masjid Kariah Chembong at 6.50pm. Four vehicles inside the workshop were also destroyed.

items.title: Mubarak mobilises veterans to support BN in Melaka election
items.summary: State BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said Mubarak was actively engaging voters through its network to garner support for the coalition. "I am grateful to Mubarak because, although they retired long ago, their fighting spirit remains strong," he said after attending the Melaka Mubarak Loyal Partners programme. Present were Mubarak president Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman and its Melaka chairman, Datuk Nazari Adzim.

items.title: Aceh worker escapes death penalty, jailed 7 years for drug possession
items.summary: Musliadi A Rahman, 40, committed the offence in 2024 and was sentenced by the High Court after pleading guilty to an alternative charge. He ordered the prison term to run from the date of Musliadi's arrest on Aug 15, 2024. "Remember, Musliadi, do not get involved in drug activities again.

items.title: Rembayung introduces new booking system to curb scalpers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Popular restaurant Rembayung has introduced a new reservation system in collaboration with Grab to curb scalping and prevent the resale of bookings. Content creator and entrepreneur Khairul Aming, whose real name is Khairul Amin Kamarulzaman, announced the changes in a Threads post, saying each verified Grab user would be limited to one reservation every two weeks. Under the new system, reservations are non-transferable.

items.title: Halal expert calls for accredited slaughterers at all poultry slaughterhouses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All slaughterhouses supplying Muslim consumers should be required to employ accredited slaughterers and halal checkers, even if they do not seek halal certification, a halal management expert said. Universiti Utara Malaysia Institute of Halal Management director Dr Nor Aina Mhd Khotib said the requirement should also apply to small operators, including roadside slaughterhouses, to ensure that trained personnel carry out slaughtering and halal checks. "Even if they do not apply for halal certification, their slaughterers should be required to have accreditation, and they should have halal checkers," she said when contacted.

items.title: Orang Asli village near KL still struggles with electricity despite solar projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — As the sun sets over Kampung Orang Asli Sg Relang, a devouring darkness comes with the stretching shadows, swallowing almost all sight and sound. Like at least 116 Orang Asli villages, according to government data in 2024, Kampung Sg Relang has mostly gone without electricity throughout the years. A view of Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Relang during a recent Bernama visit.

items.title: Pakatan files police report against BN’s Rim candidate over alleged use of govt assets in Melaka campaign, evidence to go to EC
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 2 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has lodged a police report against Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the 16th Melaka state election, Datuk Khaidirah Abu Zahar, over allegations that she campaigned using government premises and machinery. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Central Leadership Council (MPP) member Siti Aishah Shaik Ismail said the police report against the incumbent for Rim state constituency was filed by a PH representative at the Jasin district police headquarters (IPD) today. Aishah said they also possess evidence showing several MPJ officials wearing attire that displayed the face of the Jasin Umno vice-chief throughout the contribution distribution event.

items.title: Police free two on bail, track more suspects with Indonesia’s help in tanker ketamine case
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director, Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, said these individuals have been identified, and efforts to locate them are underway to assist with further investigations. “We recently arrested two individuals, but their remand period has since expired. Commenting on the case of a Chinese national detained at Hong Kong International Airport on suspicion of transporting two kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine from Penang, Hussein noted that the drug syndicate appears to have shifted away from using Malaysian citizens.

items.title: Investment, love and job scams: Nine locals among 141 arrested as Penang police bust 14 online call centres
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Penang police arrested 141 individuals, including nine locals, in 14 raids on call centres suspected of conducting various online scam operations in the state from October 9 to 29. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the state Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) operation involved five raids in Timur Laut district, six in Barat Daya district, and three in Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT), following intelligence gathering and surveillance. Lim said police also seized equipment, including mobile phones, laptops, tablets, internet routers, electronic equipment and computer accessories, believed to be used in the syndicates’ operations, valued at RM1.4 million.

items.title: Police rule out racial, gang links in Desa Tun Razak clash; seek 15 more suspects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police have ruled out racial and gang-related elements in an altercation involving a group of individuals outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, last night. Cheras police chief ACP Mohd Rosdi Daud said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a business turf dispute, although investigations were ongoing to establish the actual cause. Earlier, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that nine people had been arrested by a team from the Sungai Besi Police Station’s Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit and the Cheras district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division.

items.title: Police arrest man at Penang airport over RM3.2m cannabis bound for London; RM1.05m drugs seized in Jelutong
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Police arrested a local man in possession of 40 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds, valued at RM3.2 million, which were allegedly being smuggled to London. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the 28-year-old man, who hails from Miri, Sarawak, was apprehended at about 5pm while in the airport’s waiting area and the drugs were discovered during an inspection of his luggage. In a separate case, Lim said police arrested three individuals, including a Chinese national woman, during a raid at an apartment in Jelutong here yesterday evening.

items.title: Operasi Payung: Education Ministry boosts flood prep for SPM candidates, says deputy D-G
items.summary: Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation was aimed at helping candidates in flood-affected areas sit for their examinations without disruption. He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations. Zainal said the ministry was also coordinating preparations with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), state and district disaster management committees and other relevant agencies to assist areas at risk of flooding.

items.title: KL to get 22km of covered walkways under RM55m project starting Jan 2027, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Putrajaya will spend RM55 million to build the covered pedestrian walkways across the capital city, with the start of work scheduled for January 2027, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh told Parliament this evening. Under Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) operating expenditure, 22 kilometres of covered walkways will be built across Kuala Lumpur’s parliamentary constituencies, with an allocation of two kilometres per constituency, she said. Yeoh said the walkways are designed to bridge critical urban gaps by connecting residential zones, public facilities, commercial hubs, bus stops, health clinics and places of worship.

items.title: Demand for ETS, EMUPlus tickets for Deepavali exceeds offered capacity as 100,304 tickets sold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has recorded the sale of 100,304 tickets for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and EMUPlus services for the Deepavali period, covering travel dates from November 5 to November 10. KTMB group chief executive officer Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the high demand reflects a positive public response to the rail services during the festive season. KTMB had previously announced an additional 14,384 seats across its ETS and EMUPlus services to meet passenger demand for the festival.

items.title: Border control agency DG Shuhaily returns to duty after leave
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 2 — The director-general of the Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, resumed his duties at the agency today, following reports that he had been on leave last week. In a post on its official Facebook page, AKPS said Mohd Shuhaily began his duties by chairing the ‘Commander’s Call’ Meeting No. Those present included AKPS deputy director-general (operations), Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M Nasir; AKPS deputy director-general (policy), Zuraini Othman; and AKPS Commander for Port Klang, Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.

items.title: Amirudin calls for stern action over alleged halal breaches at Puchong chicken plant
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 2 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has called for stern action, including prosecution, against the operator or owner of a chicken processing plant that recently sparked concern among the Muslim community. He said local authorities and halal certification bodies must strengthen cooperation in monitoring such premises, conducting investigations and gathering information from the public. Also present were Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzil Ahmad and Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) director Datuk Shahzihan Ahmad, who joined Amirudin in distributing 1,321 food packs under the Nutrisi Selangor (NutriSel) programme.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms and heavy rain to lash all 13 states, three Federal Territories until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds are forecast across all 13 states and three Federal Territories until 7pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In Perak, the affected areas include Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Selama, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Kerian, Larut, Matang, and Manjung. Similar conditions are forecast in the East Coast states of Kelantan (Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, and Jeli), Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, and Hulu Terengganu), and Pahang (Kuantan, Pekan, Jerantut, Maran, Rompin, and Cameron Highlands).

items.title: Four days of hybrid lectures from Nov 9 to 13 for IPG trainees during Deepavali, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The Education Ministry (MOE) will provide four days of hybrid lectures for trainee teachers at Institute of Teacher Education (IPG) campuses in conjunction with Deepavali. “Through this arrangement, trainee teachers returning home to celebrate Deepavali can continue attending lectures online. Fadhlina also extended her Deepavali greetings to all trainee teachers and their families celebrating the festival.

items.title: Police record Penang assemblyman’s statement over alleged assault on wife
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Penang police have confirmed receiving a report from the wife of an assemblyman who alleged that she was assaulted by her husband at their residence here last Saturday. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said police were conducting further investigations into the incident, with an investigation paper opened under Section 323 of the Penal Code. Lim also denied claims by the assemblyman’s wife that police had failed to take action on the report she lodged.

items.title: Mall manager, father file police reports over woman’s alleged harassment at KL shopping mall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police have received two reports concerning three incidents involving a woman accused of harassing visitors at a shopping mall here. Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the first report was lodged by the building manager at 7.59 pm yesterday following complaints that the woman had caused public disturbance. Ahmad Azwan said police viewed seriously any acts of violence, threats or harassment against members of the public, particularly those involving children’s safety.

items.title: No licence: Cops probe driver as three family members killed, teenage girl seriously injured in Tawau crash
items.summary: TAWAU, Nov 2 — Three members of a family were killed while a 15-year-old girl was seriously injured after the car they were travelling in skidded off the road at Batu 14, Jalan Apas, here at about 9.30am today. Tawau police chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh said the deceased were a 50-year-old woman and her two sons, aged 30 and 28, who were pronounced dead at the scene at 10.16am. He said the family was travelling from Kampung Bahagia, Sandakan, to Tawau when the 28-year-old son, who was driving, allegedly lost control of the car along a straight stretch of road.

items.title: Anwar: Govt boosts MAF senior officers’ career paths in recognition of their role
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The government has agreed to improve the career progression of senior Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) officers in recognition of their heavy responsibilities in defending national sovereignty and security, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the agreement was reached during a special meeting with MAF’s top leadership, which he chaired today. Anwar said he valued direct input and feedback from the MAF leadership, emphasising that every government policy and decision must be based on actual needs on the ground rather than mere considerations on paper.

items.title: Klang Valley flash floods hit Denai Alam, TTDI, Bukit Jalil, Subang and more
items.summary: Videos and photographs shared on social media showed flooding in Denai Alam, Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI), Bukit Jalil, Subang and along the Federal Highway near Amcorp Mall in Petaling Jaya. In Denai Alam, Threads user @iskandarsukandar shared footage of heavy rain reducing visibility, with several motorists apparently turning back. Is Denai Alam flooded?”

items.title: No unhealthy API readings as monsoon winds to cut transboundary haze, improve air quality, says DOE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Air quality is expected to improve further amid increasingly humid conditions and more frequent rainfall in several areas, as well as a downgrade in regional haze alert levels by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC). Azuri Azizah said the DOE’s latest monitoring showed that air quality in most parts of Malaysia was improving. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 39 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings as of 3pm today, while 29 areas recorded good air quality.

items.title: Teoh Beng Hock family knew for seven years death wasn’t probed as murder, court told
items.summary: Senior Federal Counsel Mohammad Sallehuddin Md Ali raised the matter in the government’s preliminary objection to the fresh judicial review application filed by Beng Hock’s family on April 17 this year. According to Mohammad Sallehuddin, the investigation into Beng Hock’s death in 2009 had actually been reclassified under Section 342 of the Penal Code for wrongful confinement in 2019. Beng Hock’s parents were present in court today.

items.title: Cheras police custodial death: Three lawyers questioned over alleged harassment of doctor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police are investigating allegations that several lawyers harassed a forensic specialist in connection with the death of detainee Noorizwan Zulkefly. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said police had received a report from the doctor and were investigating the case under Sections 506, 186 and 189 of the Penal Code. He said police had so far recorded statements from the doctor and three lawyers linked to the case, while statements from Noorizwan’s family members were being taken.

items.title: Fire partially destroys KTMB cargo train in Johor Bahru, no casualties reported
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 2 — A Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) cargo train was partially damaged by a fire while travelling at Kilometre 4.75 near Taman Daya here today. Tebrau Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Nor Azmi Maryono said the train was travelling from Kempas Baru station to Pasir Gudang station when the incident occurred. Firefighters work to extinguish a fire involving a Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) cargo train locomotive near Taman Daya in Johor Bahru on November 2, 2026.

items.title: No need to stockpile food, Malaysia has at least six months of supply, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Malaysia has sufficient food supply capacity for at least six months and sees no need for emergency stockpiling measures despite concerns over potential disruptions to essential supplies, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the government continued to ensure national food security and adequate supplies of essential goods for Malaysians and others residing in the country. Ahmad Zahid was responding to reports that several countries had advised their citizens to stockpile food and essential supplies in preparation for possible emergencies.

items.title: AirAsia advises guests to plan ahead as year-end travel peak meets monsoon season
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 2 — AirAsia has advised guests travelling during the year-end peak travel period to plan ahead and allow sufficient time for their journeys amid increased passenger traffic and potentially adverse weather conditions. “Guests are encouraged to stay informed and take the necessary precautions before travelling,” it said in a statement today, while recommending all guests take note of the following advisory. “All guests, including those travelling under group bookings, are strongly encouraged to complete self check-in via the AirAsia MOVE app or our airasia.com.

items.title: Two friends plead not guilty to attempted RM8.2m jewellery robbery in Brickfields
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Two friends pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to attempting to rob a jewellery supplier of valuables worth RM8.2 million last month. Salesman Tan Kah Seng, 35, and mechanic Tan Chien Ann, 30, were jointly charged with attempting to rob Toung Zheng Fay, 30, of three bags containing various types of jewellery while armed with a machete in front of a hotel in Brickfields at 10am on October 14. Section 393 carries a maximum jail term of seven years and a fine, while Section 397 provides for imprisonment of up to 14 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.

items.title: Long-term solution needed for Langkawi ferry lane sedimentation, says Loke
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 2 — The issue of sedimentation along the ferry lane in the waters of Kuala Kedah requires a more sustainable, long-term solution to ensure the smooth operation of ferry services to Langkawi. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said dredging works are carried out periodically every two years to prevent sedimentation from disrupting operations in the area. Regarding the development of the new Kuala Kedah passenger terminal slated for completion in September 2027 he said the facility is expected to enhance the operational capacity of ferry services at the terminal.

items.title: Document public sector expertise, institutional knowledge before it is lost, says public service chief
items.summary: Public Service Director-General (KPPA) Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said knowledge gained through administrative work and research should be preserved and translated into policies, decisions and practical measures. “Documented experience becomes institutional knowledge that builds the collective memory of the public service,” he said in his keynote address at the opening of the 2026 Research Colloquium at the National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN) here today. Wan Ahmad Dahlan urged government agencies to document project implementation experiences and administrative challenges through case studies and action research findings.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan challenges MCA to debates in all four seats they contest
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 2 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has proposed holding open debates with Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates from MCA contesting four seats in the 16th Melaka state election, expanding a challenge initially directed at its candidate for the Banda Hilir seat. PH Melaka deputy chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said the proposal followed MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong’s challenge to the PH candidate for Banda Hilir to hold a debate in the constituency. Meanwhile, Lee said PH had also proposed debates involving the top leadership of both parties to discuss national policies affecting Melaka.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng urges Penang govt to freeze tax hikes, scrutinise major projects
items.summary: Debating the 2027 Supply Bill and Development Estimates in the Penang State Legislative Assembly today, Lim said he supported the RM1.074 billion state budget, noting that the Consolidated Revenue Account balance had increased from RM522.87 million at the end of 2025 to RM651.28 million as at October 30 this year, while Penang’s gross domestic product grew 7.3 per cent to RM130.3 billion in 2025, compared with national growth of 5.2 per cent. Lim also welcomed the appointment of new state secretary Datuk Dr Jafri Abdul Jalil, effective August 3, 2026, and thanked his predecessor Datuk Seri Zulkifli Long for his service. On water supply, Lim urged the state government to table its bulk water supply agreement with Perak’s Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd in the state assembly for debate and approval, saying the 40-year arrangement from 2032 carried an estimated cost of RM24.6 billion up to 2072, comprising RM8.4 billion in infrastructure capacity charges and RM16.2 billion in water supply charges; he said the agreement should be made public and that the state should seek Perak’s consent to disclose its terms even if a non-disclosure agreement was in place, as Penang residents would ultimately bear the cost.

items.title: Penang studies Third Link bridge as alternative to undersea tunnel, will seek port commission feedback
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — The state government is still conducting a conceptual design study for the proposed Penang Third Link Bridge as an alternative to the undersea tunnel, before presenting it to the Penang Port Commission (PPC) for feedback. State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the state government had approved a realignment study based on a bridge design concept, taking into consideration plans to expand Penang Port and the need to ease traffic congestion in Gurney Bay and its surrounding areas. He said the proposed realignment involved shifting the route northwards to ensure it was compatible with Penang Port's expansion plans, while avoiding any disruption to port operations and vessel navigation routes.
